prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1008; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured reports the other vehicle stopped abruptly and was struck from behind. Policy verified as active. Assigned to field adjuster for vehicle inspection and statement.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from the claimant. Claimant reports neck stiffness and lower back pain beginning the morning after the collision. Claimant states they did not seek emergency treatment but plans to visit their primary care provider. Claimant confirms no attorney has been retained at this time. Adjuster explained the claims process and the right to obtain independent advice.

Entry 3: Photos of both vehicles received and reviewed. Rear bumper and trunk damage visible on claimant vehicle, consistent with the reported impact. Estimate requested from an approved repair facility. Police report number obtained from the responding agency and requested for file.

Entry 4: Medical authorization form sent to claimant with a request for records from the treating provider. Claimant returned the signed form. Diagnosis on initial visit noted as cervical and lumbar strain with prescribed physical therapy referral. Reserve adjusted to reflect current injury information.

Entry 5: Follow-up call placed to claimant to confirm treatment progress and reminder of pending records. Claimant reports ongoing neck and back discomfort but is attending physical therapy. No demand package received. Claimant remains unrepresented. File diary set for next review.
